result.title: Self-Rewarded Reinforcement Learning for Better-Structured Medical Explanations in Small Language Models
result.summary: Small language models (SLMs) can run on commodity hardware and support privacy-preserving, on-premises clinical deployment, but their medical explanations are often short and poorly structured compared with large language models. Recent supervised approaches such as Meerkat transfer chain-of-thought reasoning into 7B-8B backbones, yet their training objective does not directly target the style or organization of the generated rationales. Building on the instruction-tuned Mistral-7B backbone, we investigate whether a lightweight reinforcement learning (RL) step can improve explanation structure without human preference labels.We apply Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with LoRA adaptation to 2,000 Meerkat-derived medical prompts, guided by a simple self-supervised reward that favors longer, lexically diverse, and well-punctuated responses while penalizing very short ones. Training for about 170 PPO steps on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU yields a stable increase in the average reward. Quantitative and qualitative comparisons show that the RL-tuned model produces longer, more organized, multi-point explanations while preserving the underlying medical content.We discuss the promise and the limitations of self-rewarded RL for shaping the style of medical explanations.

AI.brief_summary: 在 Mistral-7B 上用 LoRA+PPO，以偏好长度、词汇多样性和标点的自监督奖励微调 2000 条医学提示，使小模型生成更长、更有条理的多点解释。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理无直接关联，但其「用表层统计量作奖励塑形」的做法可供核查：此类长度与格式奖励若迁入 latent 推理轨迹训练，可能诱发长度偏置而非真正改善推理状态。
